items.summary: CFO recommendation: maintain containment and approve no new spend, monetization expansion, or implementation admissions this cycle. Revenue evidence supports only $4.92 aggregate Amazon commission for 2026-09-21, tied to 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, and 6 shipped items; all $4.92 is unattributed to sites, so site revenue, contribution margin, ROI, payback, and causal lift are unsupported. AI usage cost is $997.52 for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30 across 5,522 calls, including 234 errors and 5 transient errors. This exceeds the observed aggregate commission by approximately 203x, but the periods and attribution boundaries differ, so it is not an ROI calculation. Preserve the existing allthingsmasonic.com CTA refinement only as a slot-gated, reportable experiment against its 61-click 2026-09-21 baseline; do not claim revenue impact. Infrastructure spend, fixed costs, marketing spend, and direct monetization costs are unavailable, so contribution margin and budget exposure cannot be calculated.

CFO disposition: do not allocate the $4.92 Amazon aggregate row to any site. Named tracking rows show site clicks but $0 site-attributed commission in the available window; the provider aggregate row cannot support site-level revenue claims. The allthingsmasonic.com CTA work may proceed only after the existing delivery slot is released, with registered affiliate clicks as the sole primary metric and attribution validity as a release guardrail.

CFO measurement boundary: cost-to-learn is not calculable from the brief because AI spend is not linked to individual experiments, requests, roles, or learning outcomes, and infrastructure/direct operating costs are absent. Minimum measurement is a dated ledger mapping provider and infrastructure cost to site, task or experiment ID, plus verified outcome status and attributable revenue. Until that exists, treat AI spend as investment exposure rather than earned revenue or margin evidence.
